checks.evidence: World Nuclear News, dated 2026-10-06, describes BANR as a 22 MWe/75 MWt high-temperature gas-cooled reactor, with two units planned for Belledune, New Brunswick.

sources.label: World Nuclear News — BWXT's BANR microreactor selected for Canadian project (2026-10-06)
sources.quote: The BANR - BWXT Advanced Nuclear Reactor - is a 22 MWe/75 MWt high-temperature gas-cooled reactor

sources.label: ANS Nuclear Newswire — BWXT's BANR selected for Canadian project (2026-10-07)
sources.quote: a 20-megawatt electric version of BANR will be deployed

checks.review: Overruled by the main session. The shipped row is the Janus / Fort Campbell configuration; ANS (2026-10-07) quotes BWXT that for Janus 'a 20-megawatt electric version of BANR will be deployed', while the 22 MWe/75 MWt figure is the Belledune (Prodigy) configuration announced 2026-10-05. Two electrical ratings of one 75 MWt core, not a stale number.

checks.claim: Research reactor; output not stated in the cited record
checks.evidence: POWER Magazine, dated 2026-07-06 (updated 2026-07-08), describes Aalo-X as the full-power 30-MWth/10-MWe sodium-cooled demonstration nuclear power plant at INL, so the cited record does state an output.
checks.correction: Zero-power critical test reactor (no power output); the separate 30 MWth / 10 MWe Aalo-X demonstration plant is slated for construction and licensing in 2027

sources.label: POWER Magazine — Aalo Atomics test reactor reaches criticality at INL (2026-07-06)
sources.quote: Aalo-X, the full-power 30-MWth/10-MWe sodium-cooled demonstration nuclear power plant at INL

checks.review: Main session narrowed the correction. The row describes the Critical Test Reactor, which the article calls 'a full-scale zero-power physics reactor'; the 30-MWth/10-MWe figure belongs to the demonstration plant the article also calls Aalo-X. The agent's correction would have assigned 10 MWe to the zero-power machine. The claim is still wrong: the cited record does state the demonstration plant's output.
